## Goal

Execute the 24-hour experiment: apply the STE100 instruction to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, let it run for 24h, measure metrics, produce comparison report, and revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add the sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (verified via grep).
2. Record exact wall-clock T0 and commit hash.
3. Run analysis at T0+24h for both [T0-24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) windows.
4. Produce comparison report at `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` with:
   - Metrics table (session count, duration, tokens, cost for both windows)
   - Delta percentages and direction for each metric
   - Notable outliers (output-token-limit errors, extreme sessions)
   - Project and model breakdown
   - One-line interpretation per metric
5. Revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (verified via grep).
6. Record revert commit hash.

## Steps

1. Start parent implementation
2. Implement child tasks first (analysis script + tests)
3. Add STE100 sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev, record T0
4. Wait 24 hours (or set reminder/automation)
5. Run analysis for baseline window [T0-24h, T0)
6. Run analysis for experiment window [T0, T0+24h)
7. Generate comparison report
8. Revert AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev
9. Record results on work item
10. Clean up worktree

## Related

Dependent on: SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (Build analysis script), SA-0MU9VT5HI001LHKY (Add tests).

data.description:
## Goal

Emit structured, queryable contention telemetry from every semaphore wait in the
paced `test` / `test-fast` / `audit` / `audit-host` namespaces, so the ceilings and
timeouts (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`) can be
tuned from counted wait distributions instead of guesswork.

## Problem statement

Today contention evidence only exists as (a) free-text log lines (`Audit slot
acquired: …`, `Implement run_tests: test slot acquired — queued_at=… wait_seconds=…`)
and (b) post-hoc scraping of pi session logs by `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`.
Both miss the two facts tuning needs most: **how often** a wait happens at all, and
**how often the bounded wait expires** (`TestConcurrencyTimeout`, the audit
"concurrency limit reached" verdict). `Semaphore.acquire()` — the single choke point
every paced consumer passes through — records nothing. Without that record, the
deadlock/starvation class tracked by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF and SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 can
regress invisibly, and every ceiling decision is an anecdote.

## Users

- **Agent operator tuning the host pools** — "When full suites start queuing again I
  want p90 wait and timeout counts per namespace, so I can decide between raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and raising `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` without guessing."
- **Agent diagnosing a stalled gate** — "When my finish gate reports `slot_busy` I want
  to know whether the pool was saturated by three other suites or whether one waiter
  held a slot for an hour, so I know whether to wait or escalate."
- **Framework maintainer** — "After changing the semaphore I want the wait distribution
  before and after, so a fairness fix is proven rather than asserted."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `Semaphore.acquire()` wait in the paced namespaces (`test`, `test-fast`, `audit`,
  `audit-host`) appends one JSON-lines event to a configurable telemetry directory, with
  the fields `event`, `namespace`, `max_workers`, `timeout_seconds`, `queued_at`,
  `acquired_at`, `wait_seconds`, `outcome` (`acquired` | `timeout`), `deadline_expired`,
  `ticket`, `pid` and an optional `consumer` label; a fail-fast acquire (`timeout=0`) and
  a re-entrant no-op emit no wait event.
- Bounded-wait expiry is recorded with the same schema: `TestConcurrencyTimeout` from
  `run_tests.py` (both lanes) and the audit `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` /
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` verdicts appear as `outcome=timeout,
  deadline_expired=true` events carrying the configured bound — with no new exception
  types and no change to concurrency semantics.
- `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` aggregates a telemetry directory into a
  deterministic human or JSON report — per-namespace event count, p50/p90/p99/max
  `wait_seconds`, timeout count and rate, and a wait-bucket (slot-saturation) histogram —
  and acquires no semaphore, touches no worklog and writes no file.
- Telemetry is off the acquire fast path and bounded: it is written once the wait
  resolves (never inside the poll loop), a single `O_APPEND` write that swallows and
  debug-logs its own errors, disabled by an env kill switch, size-rotated with a retained
  previous file, and isolated in tests so the host-wide pool and telemetry file are never
  touched (`PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` / telemetry-dir overrides).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the
  event schema, the kill switch, the summary commands, and a worked "how to tune which env
  var from which number" procedure; the new behaviour is covered by unit tests (semaphore
  emission, expiry schema, aggregation over synthetic fixtures) and the full project test
  suite passes.

## Impact

Operators can see how long test and audit runs actually queue and how often they give up
waiting, instead of guessing which concurrency ceiling or timeout to change.

## Constraints

- **No latency on the acquire path.** Nothing may be written inside the retry loop;
  the event is emitted after the wait resolves (acquired or expired). One append per
  wait, no fsync, no floating-point formatting loops.
- **Fail-open, always.** A telemetry error (read-only dir, disk full, unparsable
  directory) is swallowed and logged at debug level — it must never change an acquire
  outcome, a run's exit status, or a cache entry.
- **No behavioural change to concurrency semantics.** Ceiling, bounded wait, jitter,
  turnstile fairness, nested-run isolation and cache-hit bypass all stay byte-identical.
  With telemetry disabled the acquire path must be indistinguishable from today.
- **No second session-log scraper.** `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K)
  already attributes waits from pi session logs and stays the historical backfill path.
  The new summary reads the JSONL stream as its primary source; it must not re-implement
  log scraping, and the two sources must never be summed together.
- **Respect the isolation contract:** telemetry honours `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` (and its own
  override), so a nested run's events never land in the host-wide pool's telemetry, and a
  test fixture spawning a nested runner is isolated automatically.
- **Bounded on disk:** append-only files grow forever otherwise; a size cap with one
  retained rotation (the `downtime-dispatches.log` precedent) keeps host hygiene.
- Framework repo boundaries: changes land in `skill/shared/`, `skill/test/`, `skill/audit/`
  and `docs/dev/`. UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — `Semaphore.acquire()` is the single choke point:
  it allocates a fairness ticket, polls the slot pool (~50 ms cadence, jittered), and
  raises `TimeoutError` at the deadline. It has no recording hook; `last_ticket` is the
  only diagnostic today.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_test_concurrency_slot()` wraps the semaphore and
  converts `TimeoutError` into `TestConcurrencyTimeout`; `paced_runner(runner, on_wait=…)`
  already reports `(queued_at, wait_seconds)` to callers, and `run_suite` records the wait
  into each result's `slot_wait_seconds`. Two lanes exist (`test` ceiling 6,
  `test-fast` ceiling 4, both bounded by `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` = 600 s, `TEST_LOCK_JITTER`
  = 0.1).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — two namespaces (`audit` admission with
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, and `audit-host` ingress with
  `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS`/`AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`); waits are reported as stderr text
  (`Audit slot acquired: … wait_seconds=…`) and never persisted.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish-gate suites route through
  `paced_runner(on_wait=_log_test_slot_wait)`, emitting another stderr line
  (`Implement run_tests: test slot acquired — …`).
- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` + `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — read-only
  post-hoc attribution over pi session logs (three call-site categories, de-duplication,
  genuine-run filter). `skill/shared/audit_gate_metrics.py` similarly scrapes logs for
  audit queue admission. Both prove the *need* for the data and the absence of an
  emission point.
- Docs `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §slot wait / §re-measuring and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` §concurrency describe the tuning knobs but give no
  telemetry-driven procedure.

## Desired change

1. **Emission in `Semaphore`** — add an opt-out telemetry recorder used by
   `acquire()`: capture `queued_at` (wall clock) and a monotonic start, then, after the
   wait resolves, append one JSONL event per wait (acquired or expired). A `timeout=0`
   fail-fast acquire and a re-entrant no-op emit nothing (they are not waits). An optional
   constructor keyword (e.g. `consumer="implement-finish"`) labels the call site; the
   label defaults to the namespace so an unlabelled producer still aggregates usefully.
2. **Timeout events with the same schema** — the expiry path in `acquire()` emits
   `outcome=timeout, deadline_expired=true`; `_test_concurrency_slot()` and the audit
   admission/ingress call sites keep raising exactly what they raise today, so
   `TestConcurrencyTimeout` and the audit "concurrency limit reached" verdict continue to
   work and gain no new fields they must interpret.
3. **Aggregation helper** — `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` reads the telemetry
   directory (`--dir`, `--since`, `--namespace`, `--json`/`--human`) and reports counts,
   p50/p90/p99/max waits, timeout counts and rates, and a saturation histogram (e.g.
   `0–1 s`, `1–10 s`, `10–60 s`, `60–300 s`, `>300 s`). Malformed lines are counted and
   skipped, never fatal. Under-sampled namespaces are labelled rather than quoted.
4. **Tuning procedure** — docs gain a table mapping each env var to the number that
   justifies changing it (e.g. high p90 with zero expiries ⇒ raise the ceiling; a
   non-trivial expiry rate with idle capacity ⇒ the bound is too short; `>300 s` waits
   with free slots ⇒ a fairness/starvation defect, not a ceiling problem).
5. **Tests** — semaphore emission (acquired, expired, fail-fast silent, re-entrant
   silent, kill switch off, telemetry failure fail-open), aggregation over synthetic
   JSONL fixtures (percentiles, histogram, timeout rate, malformed lines, empty dir), and
   an isolation test proving a nested-run directory keeps its events out of the host pool.

Documented assumptions (to confirm or correct in review):

- **Default telemetry location** — a `contention/` subdirectory of the semaphore base dir
  (`<PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR or XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores>/contention`), overridable with an
  explicit env var so the host can point it at persistent storage. Reusing the semaphore
  base gives tests and nested runs isolation for free; the trade-off is that the runtime-dir
  default does not survive a reboot, which the docs call out and the override fixes.
- **Kill switch name/shape** — an opt-out boolean env var (e.g. `PI_CONTENTION_TELEMETRY=0`)
  rather than opt-in, because AC1 requires every wait to be recorded by default.
- **One event per wait, not per poll** — a poll-cadence event stream would be orders of
  magnitude larger and would itself perturb the herd behaviour it measures.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Telemetry perturbs what it measures.** A write per *poll* would multiply the I/O of a
  saturated herd; the design records one event per *wait*, after it resolves. Residual
  risk: a host with hundreds of short waits gains hundreds of appends — mitigated by the
  single-`O_APPEND` write, the size cap, and the kill switch.
- **Disk growth / lost history.** An unbounded append file fills a runtime tmpfs; a
  rotation cap with one retained file bounds it. Conversely the default location may not
  survive a reboot, so a host that wants multi-day tuning data must set the override —
  documented, not silently assumed.
- **Test-suite cost and pollution.** Default-on emission means every isolate-and-acquire
  test in the suite writes a file. Mitigation: the telemetry dir follows the semaphore
  base dir (already a `tmp_path` in existing fixtures), the suite asserts a nested run
  stays isolated, and a test proves the kill switch and fail-open paths add no failure
  mode to the acquire path.
- **Double counting with the existing measurement.** Wait data now exists in three places
  (JSONL events, stderr lines, session logs). The constraint is explicit: the JSONL stream
  is the primary source, stderr lines stay for human log continuity, and
  `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` remains the historical backfill — never summed.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent opportunities surfaced during context gathering — automatic
  nested-run isolation (SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF), a second aggregation front-end for the audit
  queue, retention dashboards — are *not* in scope; they stay linked work items.
- **Assumption:** the semaphore is genuinely the single choke point. If a consumer acquires
  a slot by another mechanism (a bespoke `flock` outside `Semaphore`), its waits will be
  invisible; the emission point is chosen because all four paced namespaces route through
  `Semaphore.acquire()`, and the aggregation's per-namespace counts would expose a gap.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — actual emission point: `acquire()` capture/emit,
  recorder helper, telemetry-dir resolution, kill switch, error swallowing; re-export the
  recorder for callers.
- `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` — new read-only aggregation CLI (JSON by default,
  `--human` summary), replacing nothing and acquiring nothing.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — existing suite; add emission,
  fail-fast-silent, kill-switch, fail-open and isolation coverage with a tmp telemetry dir.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_contention_summary.py` — new fixture-driven aggregation tests.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_test_concurrency_slot()` / `paced_runner()` pass a
  `consumer` label per lane and prove `TestConcurrencyTimeout` still surfaces unchanged.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — label the `audit` admission and `audit-host`
  ingress acquisitions; keep verdict text unchanged.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — label the finish-gate paced runner (its
  `on_wait` line stays for log continuity).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — event schema, kill switch, summary commands, tuning
  table; cross-reference (not re-scrape) `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — the same for `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` /
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG — test-skill shared concurrency primitive (defines the ceiling,
  the bounded wait and `TestConcurrencyTimeout`).
- SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF — multi-agent audit/test coordination: the deadlock class this
  telemetry makes observable.
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 — nested-run semaphore isolation: the `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` contract
  telemetry must honour (and, still open as SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF, the item that would make
  isolation automatic).
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 — pacing telemetry: the `on_wait` hook and its `slot_wait_seconds`
  reporting; this item supplies the persisted stream beneath it.
- SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD — staggered back-off/jitter: a fairness change whose before/after
  distributions this telemetry should make measurable.
- Arrival-ordered turnstile (cited as SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI in the
  `process_semaphore.py` docstring; that id lives outside this worklog store) — slot
  fairness/starvation, whose queue-position waits are the `>300 s` bucket the summary
  reports.
- SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV — full/fast lane split (why `test-fast` must be in scope, not just
  `test`).
- SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0 — dynamic slot discovery (a ceiling symptom this telemetry would
  have caught earlier).
- SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K — `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, the existing read-only
  session-log measurement this item must not duplicate.
- SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z — finish-gate classification that reports slot wait separately; the
  consumer of the same measurement.
- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM / SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE — audit bounded priority queue and its tuning
  (the audit-side numbers this telemetry would supply directly).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No operator questions were required: every open point was resolved by inspecting the
repository, and each remaining decision is recorded above as a **documented assumption**
with its trade-off so a producer can correct it in review.

- **Q1 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Does an emission point already exist, or does
  telemetry already persist anywhere? **Answer:** No. `Semaphore.acquire()` records
  nothing; `paced_runner(on_wait=…)` only hands `(queued_at, wait_seconds)` to the caller,
  which logs a stderr line and folds the value into each result's `slot_wait_seconds`.
  Evidence: `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::Semaphore.acquire`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::paced_runner`, `…::run_suite`.
- **Q2 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Is this a duplicate of the existing measurement
  harness? **Answer:** No. `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` is a *post-hoc* parser over pi
  session logs (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) with a genuine-run filter; it cannot see waits that
  produced no log line and cannot see expiry at all. This item adds the *emission* side and
  a summary over that stream; the constraint "no second session-log scraper" keeps the two
  from diverging. Evidence: `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py`,
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §"Re-measuring post-fix slot wait".
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Which namespaces must be covered? The seed AC1
  names `test` and `audit`. **Answer:** Four exist and all four are tuning knobs:
  `test` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`), `test-fast` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, split in
  SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV — the lane partial runs actually wait in), `audit`
  (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`) and `audit-host`
  (`AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS`/`AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`). Recording at the `Semaphore` level
  covers all four for free; the ACs name them explicitly so no lane is silently skipped.
  Evidence: `run_tests.py` constants and `_lane_semaphore_config`, `audit_runner.py`
  `AUDIT_SEMAPHORE_NAME` / `AUDIT_HOST_SEMAPHORE_NAME`.
- **Q4 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Where should the telemetry file live?
  **Answer:** Under the semaphore base directory by default, because that is the directory
  tests and nested runs already isolate via `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`
  (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::nested_semaphore_dir`, docs §"Nested-run isolation");
  an explicit override lets a host keep it on persistent storage. The persistence
  trade-off is recorded as an assumption, not silently chosen.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF** – Automatic nested-run semaphore isolation: replace opt-in PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR convention with an inherited marker (open)
- **SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD** – Test semaphore: staggered back-off under contention to prevent thundering-herd waits (completed)
- **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** – Residual post-fix slot waits still breach parent thresholds (re-measurement follow-up) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mtg5ryh8005rqnm, 0mtg5u75a001f1rg, 0muszjrb9006zche, ac1, acceptance (+476 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0muy6u05f008rg86, 0mvsjx5hs002djhi, 0mvtet8kq0031r6z, absence, ac1 (+462 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mtg5u75a001f1rg, 0mua8bsag000yza2, 0mvsjx5hs002djhi, 0mvtet8kq0031r6z, absence (+457 more)

data.description:
# Add a session-time-analysis skill ("where does Pi time go") and weave it into agent-log-review

## Objective

Formalise the ad-hoc 2026-10-21 AI_Hell time-attribution methodology (throwaway
scripts in `/tmp/pi_time/`) into a maintained, globally-installed skill under
`skill/` that deterministically answers "where does Pi time go" for any project,
and share its session parser + signal extractors with agent-log-review so its
reports gain a "Where the time went" section — without weakening privacy.

## Problem statement

Operators cannot see where agent-hours go without writing throwaway scripts:
the 2026-10-21 analysis of 25 AI_Hell sessions showed ~8.7 h of ~11.8 h active
wall-clock blocked in `wait_for_job.py` (37 waits, avg ~15 min), a 2.8 h hung
`evaluate.mjs` (mis-bucketed under "git" by a naive classifier), ~1.4 h of test
runs, and >96% of ~123 M tokens as cache reads. That methodology lives in
`/tmp/pi_time/` (lost on reboot); this item makes it a repeatable skill and
weaves its metric extractors into agent-log-review so the diagnosis becomes a
standard, deterministic report section.

## Users

- **Agent operator / producer** — runs one command per project and gets a
  deterministic time-attribution report (window, session counts by kind,
  active vs blocked vs LLM vs tool, per-session and per-theme) plus waste
  flags (long blocked waits, hung commands, error-heavy tools, retry loops).
- **Maintainer of agent-log-review** — reuses the shared v3 JSONL parser and
  signal extractors so time analysis is consistent with pattern analysis.
- **Automation users** — consume `--json` output and `--parent-id` worklog
  integration for dashboards and automated reporting.

### Example user stories

- As an operator I want to run one command per project and get a deterministic
  time-attribution report (window, session count by kind, active vs blocked vs
  LLM vs tool, per-session and per-theme) so I can see where agent-hours go
  without writing throwaway scripts.
- As an operator I want the same skill to flag waste (long blocked waits, hung
  commands, error-heavy tools, retry loops) so I can act on the biggest time
  sinks.
- As a maintainer of agent-log-review I want the v3 JSONL session parser and
  signal extractors shared and reused so time analysis is consistent with
  pattern analysis, and reports gain a "Where the time went" section.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new skill under `skill/session-time-analysis/` with `SKILL.md` plus
   `scripts/` and `tests/` following agent-log-review's structure; a
   deterministic CLI with every flag documented in `--help`.
2. Report covers: window, session count by kind (e.g. audit vs interactive),
   union **and** naive-sum active wall time with the double-counting
   distinction explained (2026-10-21: sum-LLM 10.0 h vs union 6.5 h), LLM vs
   tool split, per-tool time/calls/errors, per-model time, token & cache
   economics (input/output/cacheRead, cache-hit %), blocking classification
   totals, and top-10 longest bash commands with hang flagging.
3. Blocking classification attributes by primary binary / first token
   (not substring match — the 2026-10-21 2.8 h `evaluate.mjs` must not land
   under "git"), flags per-command-family duration outliers as hung, and
   surfaces the top-N longest commands.
4. Union (de-duplicated across concurrent sessions) and naive-sum figures are
   both reported and explained; timezone-correct day windowing, sessions
   spanning midnight, and malformed lines degrade without crashing.
5. agent-log-review reports gain the time-attribution section sourced from the
   shared extractors, and its classification prompt receives time/waste
   signals; privacy/redaction guarantees are preserved (raw logs never sent to
   a model, secrets redacted).
6. Automated tests cover parser/metrics edge cases (malformed lines,
   midnight-spanning sessions, millisecond vs ISO timestamps, empty dir,
   missing usage degrade, no crash) and a golden fixture from the 2026-10-21
   AI_Hell sessions asserting the headline figures (~8.7 h blocked-wait of
   ~11.8 h active; hung tune run 2.78 h; test runs ~1.4 h). Tests run under
   the repo's test policy (test skill).
7. `SKILL.md` documents usage, metric definitions, limitations (provider
   durationMs may skew under slot contention; host-load correlation initially
   out of scope), and the integration contract with agent-log-review.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g.
   `docs/dev/session-time-analysis-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators can run one deterministic command per project to see exactly where
agent-hours go (blocked waits, hung commands, tokens) and get the same
diagnosis automatically inside agent-log-review reports — no throwaway scripts.

## Constraints

- Skills live in `skill/<name>/` with `scripts/` and `tests/`; global install
  via `scripts/install_pi.sh` (symlink of `skill/` → `~/.pi/agent/skills`);
  changes affect every project, so they are tracked here, built, tested, and
  pushed to `dev` before re-install.
- **Privacy:** raw session logs are never sent to a model and never persisted;
  secrets remain redacted (mirror agent-log-review's guarantees).
- Deterministic output: same input directory + flags ⇒ byte-identical report
  (stable ordering, no randomness).
- UK English throughout; follow existing skill conventions and the shared
  test-writing guidelines (avoid self-referential simulations — the golden
  fixture reproduces 2026-10-21 *metrics*, it does not reimplement game logic).
- v3 JSONL session format assumed stable (fields: `session`, `model_change`,
  `thinking_level_change`, `message` with content parts, `toolResult`,
  `usage`, `durationMs`, ISO and/or epoch-ms timestamps).
- Do not depend on the `/tmp/pi_time/` throwaway scripts long-term (gone on
  reboot); the SKILL.md metric definitions are the source of truth.

## Existing state

- Throwaway analysis scripts `/tmp/pi_time/{analyse,deep,final,theme,content}.py`
  (currently deleted; do not depend on them — reference the recorded metrics in
  this item's description instead).
- Session logs at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` (v3 format);
  the 2026-10-21 AI_Hell sample dataset still exists (41 files) and is the
  golden-fixture source.
- agent-log-review skill exists: `skill/agent-log-review/` (SKILL.md,
  `scripts/agent_log_review.py` with `parse_session`/`read_sessions`/session
  dir resolution, `tests/`); epic SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC.
- Related completed parser work: SA-0MV6U4PW4007R7FE (v3 JSONL parser),
  SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (one-off ste100 `analyze_sessions.py`).
- 2026-11-13 re-evaluation of 36 AI_Hell implement-skill sessions reproduced
  the pattern (668 min summed vs 388 min wall-clock; 37% in wait_for_job;
  88–93% of long-session time inside bash waits) — filed as epic
  SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1; this skill should reproduce those metrics
  deterministically.

## Desired change

Create `skill/session-time-analysis/` (SKILL.md + `scripts/` + `tests/`) with a
deterministic CLI (`--json`, `--output-file`, `--cwd`/`--session-root`,
`--max-sessions`, optional `--parent-id` worklog integration mirroring
agent-log-review's idempotent comments). Factor the v3 session parser and
signal extraction into shared modules consumed by both this skill and
agent-log-review; extend agent-log-review's distilled signals with
time/blocking/waste features, add the time-attribution report section, and add
a time-waste category to its classification prompt — preserving its privacy
guarantees.

Deliberate improvements over the throwaway scripts: union (de-duplicated) vs
naive-sum metrics; primary-binary/first-token blocking attribution with
duration-outlier hang flagging; per-command-family outlier detection; surfaced
top-N longest commands; timezone-correct day windowing; malformed-line
degradation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/session-time-analysis/SKILL.md` — skill definition, usage, metric definitions, limitations, integration contract
- `skill/session-time-analysis/scripts/session_time_analysis.py` — deterministic CLI + report renderer (Markdown/JSON)
- `skill/session-time-analysis/scripts/__init__.py` — package marker (mirror agent-log-review)
- `skill/session-time-analysis/tests/test_session_time_analysis.py` — parser/metrics edge cases
- `skill/session-time-analysis/tests/test_golden_2026_10_21.py` — golden fixture on the AI_Hell sample dataset (or a checked-in fixture snapshot)
- `skill/session-time-analysis/tests/conftest.py` — fixtures (mirror agent-log-review)
- Shared extraction module(s) consumed by both skills — e.g. `skill/shared/session_logs.py` + `skill/shared/session_time_metrics.py` (or a `session_time_analysis/` shared package), to be confirmed at plan time
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — modified to use the shared extractors and emit the time-attribution section + time-waste signals
- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — updated for the new section/signals
- `docs/dev/session-time-analysis-skill-reference.md` — skill reference docs
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — no change needed (installs `skill/` wholesale); verify

## Related work

- **SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC** — Agent log review skill: analyse session logs for repeated confusion patterns (epic; the skill this item integrates with).
- **SA-0MV6U4PW4007R7FE** — Agent log review: session log parser (v3 JSONL format) (completed; parser this item shares/extends).
- **SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY** — Build analysis script for ste100-24h experiment (completed; one-off analysis script, partial overlap on token/duration metrics).
- **SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD** — 24h experiment: measure session length & token use (open; related measurement context).
- **SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1** — Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (in-progress epic; consumed a 2026-11-13 session-time-style measurement — this skill should reproduce those metrics).
- **SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E** — Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out (blocked; measurement methodology overlap).
- **SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E** — Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts (completed; wait_for_job is the dominant blocked time sink this skill measures).

## Risks & assumptions

**Assumptions**
- v3 session log format is stable enough for parsing (fields as in the current
  files); `durationMs` reflects per-call LLM time subject to provider/slot
  variance.
- Default window is the most recent day (local timezone) for which sessions
  exist, overridable via CLI window flags; exact default confirmed at plan
  time (assumption documented here because the seed context did not pin it).
- The 2026-10-21 AI_Hell sessions remain readable at their current path for
  the golden fixture (41 files verified present); if `--session-root` is
  unavailable at test time, snapshot a redacted fixture into `tests/`.
- Shared extraction modules live under `skill/shared/` (or a
  `skill/session-time-analysis/` importable package) — exact location
  confirmed at plan time; agent-log-review's existing parser is factored out
  without behaviour change.

**Risks & mitigations**
- **Provider durationMs skew** — LLM `durationMs` may under/over-state under
  slot contention; report it as approximate and document the limitation (AC7).
- **Misclassification regression** — naive substring blocking attribution
  mis-bucketed the 2026-10-21 hung node run under "git"; AC3 mandates
  primary-binary/first-token attribution plus a regression test.
- **Privacy regression** — adding time/waste signals to agent-log-review must
  not leak raw log content; AC5 pins the redaction/no-raw-log guarantees and
  tests cover the classification prompt input.
- **Golden fixture drift** — if session files change/rotate, the fixture
  becomes stale; mitigate with a checked-in redacted snapshot plus the metric
  assertions (not byte-for-byte log equality).
- **Scope creep** — host-load correlation, live monitoring, and automated
  remediation are out of scope; record any such opportunities as linked work
  items, not additions here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required — the seed context (description with
user stories, design points, six acceptance criteria, context & references,
and a sample dataset with headline figures) suffices to draft a clear brief.
Open items recorded as assumptions above:
- Q: "Default analysis window when no window flags are supplied?" — Answer
  (agent assumption, needs plan-time confirmation): most recent day (local
  timezone) with session data, overridable via CLI flags. Research: the
  2026-10-21 analysis windowed by day (00:52–18:54 local); agent-log-review
  bounds by most-recent-20-sessions, so a "most recent day" default is
  consistent with both. Source: seed description (day-windowing) + sample
  dataset.
- Q: "Where do the shared parser/extractor modules live?" — Answer (agent
  assumption, needs plan-time confirmation): `skill/shared/` or a package
  importable by both skills; agent-log-review's existing parser factored out
  without behaviour change. Research: `skill/shared/` already hosts
  cross-skill helpers (status_lifecycle.py, wait_for_job.py, tree_coverage.py,
  process_semaphore.py); agent_log_review.py currently embeds
  `parse_session`/`read_sessions`. Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Is the golden fixture checked into tests/ or read live?" — Answer
  (agent assumption, needs plan-time confirmation): prefer a redacted checked-in
  snapshot so tests are hermetic; the live 2026-10-21 AI_Hell files are the
  source for producing it. Research: 41 files verified present under
  `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell--/2026-10-21*`.
  Source: filesystem inspection.

data.description:
# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** transferred from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine
> store) by producer decision, where it was `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`
> (TCE worktree `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`,
> commit `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree. The CG item is
> deleted after transfer; the full intake brief lives here.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix lands in this repository.** The defective code is
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` here; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `skill/`. Do **not** edit another project's `.pi/`, and do not create a
  vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (this repo).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (Tableau-Card-Engine checkout, registered worktree, git toplevel =
  the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>   (historical reproduction in a sibling project)
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (this repository, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory**
  so the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect, **filed separately** by producer decision as
  `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` (see *Related work*):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line
  ~48) duplicates the ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"`
  construction and no initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()`
  would read `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 258)
  gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the same helper instead of its
  own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the "`StatusLifecycle` resolves the same
  directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the initialised-only /
  no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — worklog-store resolution note
  (~lines 360–364).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` — `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's
  non-initialised `.worklog` (the same walk duplicated in `code_freeze.py`).
  Filed separately by producer decision (Appendix Q2) and **blocked by** this
  item, so the shared rule lands first.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — original discovery work item.
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (Tableau-Card-Engine, completed) — earlier
  worktree-resolution defect (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree):
  same failure family, different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Excluded by
  producer decision (Appendix Q2) — it is filed separately.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix and its record land?** The defective code lives
  in SorraAgents (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no
  `skill/` tree, so a TCE `implement.py` worktree could not carry the change
  (the TCE-side `implement.py finish` fails closed on out-of-worktree edits).
  Options were: (a) transfer the item to the SA store; (b) create an SA item
  carrying code + tests, keep the CG item as a linked discovery record;
  (c) commit to SorraAgents `dev` from outside a worktree (breaks
  worktree-isolation). Agent recommendation: (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"SA create there then delete this item"* — create the
  SA item with the full brief (this item) **and delete** the CG item, i.e. a
  transfer rather than a linked pair. Source: operator reply in the intake
  session `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q2 — Fold in the adjacent `code_freeze.py` defect?** Options: (a) fix both
  in this change via one shared helper; (b) keep this item narrow and file the
  `code_freeze` fix as a separate `discovered-from` item. Agent recommendation:
  (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — the `code_freeze.py`

# Test-first: `start` base-ref harness and current-behaviour characterisation

Build the executable test harness for `start`'s worktree base-ref resolution
(parent item **SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK**), plus characterisation coverage of the
behaviour that must survive the fix. This item lands **green**; the new
behaviour's red-first cases are written inside the implementation child
(SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX), because a committed red tree cannot be pushed — the
`finish` changed-scope gate requires a passing suite.

## Test file

`skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py` (new). Reuse the hermetic
patterns already in this package: a real temporary git repo with a bare `origin`
(see `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py`'s `git_repo` fixture) plus
patched-boundary helpers (see `test_phase_start_claim.py`'s `_mocked_phase_start`).

## Deliverables

1. **Diverged-base fixture**: a builder that creates a repo where `origin/dev`
   has advanced past a stale, diverged local `dev` (e.g. `ahead 1, behind 1`),
   overridable for `behind`-only, `ahead`-only, dirty-checkout and
   lock-held scenarios. Exported as a reusable helper for the implementation
   child's cases.
2. **Characterisation tests (green today)**:
   - a behind-only local `dev` with a skipped refresh (lock held; and separately a
     dirty main checkout) still lets `start` succeed — fail open;
   - a failed `git fetch origin dev` still lets `start` succeed and forks from the
     local branch;
   - `start` never force-updates or moves a diverged local `dev` (its tip is
     unchanged after the call);
   - the created worktree branch tracks `origin/dev` (`branch.<new>.remote` /
     `branch.<new>.merge`), because `finish` pushes to `origin/dev`.
3. **Base-ref assertion helpers**: worktree merge-base with
   `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, and a `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]` reader that
   is tolerant today (absent → clearly skipped/xfail-free assertion helper
   introduced by the implementation child, not a placeholder test).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py` exists and its
  characterisation tests (behind-only skip, fetch failure, no force-update,
  upstream tracking) pass against the current implementation.
- **AC2** — The reusable diverged-base fixture covers the diverged, behind-only,
  ahead-only, dirty-checkout and lock-held scenarios and is exercised by at least
  one green test per scenario.
- **AC3** — No test is committed red, skipped, or marked xfail in this item; the
  new behaviour's failing cases are added by SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX.
- **AC4** — No production code under `skill/implement/scripts/` is modified by this
  item.
- **AC5** — The new file passes via the test skill (`/skill:test`) as part of the
  `skill/implement` changed scope.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`

## Impact

The stale-base defect gets an executable harness and its current fail-open
behaviour is pinned, so the fix can be specified red-first without ever pushing a
red tree.

# Race-clobber restore regression tests

Parent: SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B (audit restore lost-update). Test-first slice: land
the regression suite for the concurrent-`wl sync` clobber **before** the fixes
(F2/F3), so each fix is proven by a red-then-green test.

## Scope

Deterministic clobber injection for the audit lifecycle restore paths: an
injectable `wl` runner/store that reverts an item to a stale
`open`/`plan_complete` snapshot at a scripted point (before the next `wl show`
readback, or after a verified readback), modelling the concurrent `wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ class).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` between the audit status change and its restore and asserts the item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` after the first verified restore readback and asserts the settle re-verification restores the item again.
- [ ] An aborted audit restores the item to `completed`/`in_review`, verified after write and retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered the restore, even when the clobber lands on the first restore write.
- [ ] A regression test raises an exception after the `in_progress` claim (audit lease / checkpoint store) and asserts the captured pre-audit state is restored, never `in_progress`.
- [ ] A JS unit test drives `checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` with a clobbered restore, asserts one bounded retry, and asserts the state file is retained when the restore cannot be verified.
- [ ] The harness (injectable runner recording every `wl update`/`wl show`, with scripted clobber points (a) before the first readback and (b) after a verified readback) lives in `skill/audit/tests/`; the suite is red pre-fix (red run recorded in a work-item comment) and green after the fixes; no duplication of existing `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` coverage.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_restore_race.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`

## Out of scope

Fixing the restore paths (children F2/F3); fixing the general `wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ).

## Objective

Add the read-only, unit-testable **bump preflight helper** used by the ship skill's new version-bump evaluation step. It gathers the release candidates and renders a compact review packet. It performs **no judgement and no mutation** — the agent judges, the producer approves.

## User Story

As the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`, I want a single helper that gathers every release candidate and renders the evidence I need to judge the release's importance, so that my patch/minor/major call is based on the items' content rather than guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- New module `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` exports a `gatherReleaseCandidates` (name may vary) that resolves candidates through an **injectable fetch boundary** (default `getCandidateItems()` from `check-audit-gate.js`); tests inject fakes and never read the live worklog.
- The helper enriches each candidate with the fields needed to judge importance: `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, the `## Impact` section or user story, and a truncated description excerpt. It tolerates missing fields (falls back to the title/id and an empty excerpt) without throwing.
- The helper renders a review packet (Markdown or plain text) that includes: the current version, the three candidate outcomes computed via the **existing** `bump-version.js` arithmetic (`bumpVersion`), and the per-item evidence listed above. It reuses `resolveVersionSource`/`bumpVersion` (no duplicated semver arithmetic).
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics (`bumpVersion`) rather than duplicating version arithmetic anywhere in the new helper.
- An **empty or unreadable candidate set** fails safe: the helper reports `patch` as the proposal, logs a warning explaining why, and never throws or blocks a release.
- Gathering/rendering is **purely read-only** — the helper performs no `git`, tag, PR, or `wl` mutation.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` covers: candidate gathering via the injected boundary, rendering of every packet field, the empty candidate set (patch + warning), and that `minor`/`major` outcomes reset the lower components correctly (delegated to `bumpVersion`).
- Tests pass via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope changed`, node suite) and touch no live worklog or real git state.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the failing test file first (`test_bump_preflight.mjs`, `node:test`).
2. Add `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` with an exported preflight function accepting `{ getCandidateItemsFn, repoRoot }` injection.
3. Project `version` from the resolved version source; compute `patch`/`minor`/`major` outcomes with `bumpVersion`.
4. Render the packet with a stable, agent-readable layout; truncate description excerpts (e.g. ~200 chars).
5. Return a structured result (`{ candidates, currentVersion, proposals, proposedBump, warning }`) as well as the rendered text, so tests can assert fields directly.
6. Export a small render/format function so the workflow contract test can rely on a stable API.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (reuse `getCandidateItems`)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` (reuse `resolveVersionSource`, `bumpVersion`)

## Constraints

- No issue-type or priority classifier — the helper only gathers/renders evidence.
- No mutation and no new git side effects.
- Empty/unreadable candidates default to `patch` with a warning.

## Deliverables

- `bump-preflight.js` with tests, passing the changed-scope suite.
data.title: Bump preflight helper: gather release candidates + review packet
